name: Cable knee extension
cue: Lean back; extend the knee, lower slowly.
research: Seated cable knee extension, right leg working, on the leg extension's reclined seat (v10, science audit A6, 4 Oct 2026: the rectus femoris grew clearly more at a hip angle of 40 deg than at 90 deg, Larsen 2025, and the deep-knee half grew more than the final half, Pedrosa 2022): pelvis reclined 40 deg with the back pad as far back as the machine goes, thighs level on the seat (hip flexion 50), the hands on the side handles at hip level. An ankle cuff (0.04 H in radius, 0.07 to 0.11 H above the ankle) on the right shank carries a ring on its back; the cable runs from the ring back under the seat to a low pulley (0.075 H, 0.10 H behind the hip joint under the back of the seat, on a long low arm from the column 0.5 H behind the seat), so it pulls the ankle back and down and the knee is straightened against it. The knee goes from 100 deg (starting from the deepest bend) to 5 deg, the ankle from 5 to 8 deg of dorsiflexion. The left leg rests with the knee at 95 deg, the foot flat on a footrest. Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial. The cable runs from the ring down to the pulley, 21 deg below horizontal at the bottom, 12 mid-range and 21 deg at the top (the moment arm against the cable, the sine of the angle between the shank and the cable, is 0.86 at the bottom, 0.90 mid-range and 0.44 at the top). Cable 1:1 to the stack. Geometry: design/cableB/ck.mjs.

targets.note: the research values of the leg extension for the seat; the cuff and cable are design values (standard technique), not a measured trial

camera.note: Research view is the lateral profile (az 90). az 80 stays 10 deg off it; raised 14 deg so the anterior thigh of the working right leg (the quads face up on the horizontal thighs) reads along its whole length, with rectus femoris between vastus lateralis and medialis, and the cable and cuff show where the load comes from. The base is a fore-aft rail, not a plate: from above a plate would run under the exercise name.

skinChecks.note: the resting left foot is flat on its rest
